expect.more: airframe.capabilities {section: appspec} FIRST when writing an AppSpec for airframe.plan/apply (every field, how config/overrides map onto chart values, a worked example); {kind} for one kind's outputs, conditions and verify checks; {section: chart|xrds|components|targets|kinds|appspec} for a whole section. This default answer is large and may be clipped: narrow with section or kind

analysisTemplates.description: App-specific Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplates, rendered in this namespace. Reference them by name from rollout.steps or rollout.canaryAnalysis; the chart does not wire them in.

appName.description: This application's name. Used as the Helm release name's basis, the default ServiceAccount name, and the default databaseName for a PostgreSQL component. A DNS-1123 label: lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, must start and end with an alphanumeric.

appType.description: app runs a workload; infra is a components-only service. A label for people and tools: the chart decides what to render from rollout.enabled, not from this.

attachedResourceApiVersion.description: The apiVersion group used to look up component/SLO XRs by componentKinds. Update here, not per-template, if the group ever changes.

autoscaling.description: HorizontalPodAutoscaler settings for the main workload.

cluster.description: This cluster's name in the cluster registry, which is also its kubectl context name. Used to name this app's SecretStores (<appName>-<cluster>) and to label what the chart renders. The ApplicationEnvironment composition writes it for Flight environments and Glidepath sets it for Ground environments; never a literal in the chart.

clusterType.description: This cluster's role, copied from its cluster-registry record's `type` (dev: the control-plane cluster that hosts Ground environments and the one shared SecretStore per app; upper: any other cluster). Decides where secrets: entries are read from. The chart compares no cluster names. Required whenever secrets: is non-empty: the render fails without it rather than guess. ApplicationEnvironment writes upper for Flight environments; Glidepath sets dev for Ground environments.

componentKinds.description: Deliberate lookup map exception: component type string -> XR kind. A new component kind needs a row here, not a template change.

components.description: Attached-tier component instances (Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, ...). Each entry's spec is validated against that component's own XRD schema by the compiled schema (airframe_schema.compiled_schema()), not by this file directly - see tools/airframe-validate.

configMaps.description: ConfigMaps mounted or projected as env vars into the main workload.

cronJobs.description: Scheduled batch tasks (nightly cleanup, report generation, ...). Share env/secrets/configMaps/volumes with the main container automatically.

env.description: Container environment variables for the main workload.

envName.description: The environment name (dev, staging, prod, or a PR number). Named envName, not env, because env is already this schema's top-level container env-var list - a same-named field would collide in one flat values map.

extraManifests.description: Last-resort escape hatch - a raw list of arbitrary Kubernetes objects, rendered as-is, no labels stamped.

httpRoute.description: Gateway API HTTPRoute, first-class alongside classic ingress. This platform's convention: <app>.<cluster-or-env-qualifier>.<fleet domain> (the fleet's own local DNS suffix; nothing here assumes one).

ingress.description: Classic Ingress. Gateway API (httpRoute below) is the mechanism most new callers actually want on this fleet's real clusters.

jobs.description: One-off batch tasks - the common 'run a DB migration before the new Rollout comes up' pattern. Same image/env/secrets/configMaps/volumes defaulting as cronJobs.

namespace.description: Extra labels/annotations stamped on this release's own Namespace object.

networkPolicy.description: Traffic policy for the main workload's namespace.

notifications.description: AI-triage diagnosis notifications, threaded into the RolloutWatch XR this chart renders unconditionally.

observability.description: The cluster's observability stack, as the tenant-onboarding ApplicationSet passes it (from Apron's cluster config and the app's kind). Empty fields turn each part off, so a cluster without the stack, or a Ground environment, renders exactly as before.

platformSecretStore.description: Unused since the release-tracking hook Jobs and their relay-token ExternalSecret were removed (glidepath ADR-0021 phase 3b); kept so existing env files that set it still validate.

podDisruptionBudget.description: Set at most one of minAvailable/maxUnavailable.

release.description: Machine-owned: written by the release pipeline (Glidepath) into the release file, never by hand in a human-owned env file. Takes precedence over the deprecated rollout.image. No workload renders (Rollout/Service/ServiceMonitor) until both release.image fields are set.

releaseTracking.description: Opaque escape hatch, deliberately excluded from the strictness rule: written by glidepath's open-release-pr.yaml, never hand-authored. Null when this env hasn't gone through a release pipeline yet. Only releaseId and appNamespace are read (glidepath ADR-0021): releaseId is rendered onto the Rollout as the hangar.io/release-id annotation, with a hangar.io/release-tracked label, so the Argo Rollouts notifications engine can report the release; appNamespace is the dev-cluster namespace of the release record. Older release files also carry relayUrl, relayHostAliasIP, configJsonB64 and other fields for the removed hook Jobs; they are ignored. Setting releaseTracking on a release with no Rollout fails the render.

rollout.description: The Argo Rollout workload. Use rollout.enabled: false for an environment with no long-running service; null is read the same way.

secrets.description: Secrets, aggregated into one app-secrets Secret via ExternalSecret/ClusterSecretStore, consumed by the main container.

kinds.summary: The durable half of an Autopilot agent, as a pin: which commit of the agent definition in the app's own repository (agents/<name>.yaml) is live. Clearance lists these XRs, fetches each pinned file through the agents' GitHub App and loads it beside the platform's bundled definitions. The XR composes nothing and carries no definition content or credential; it is requested through the Autopilot templates in Backstage (New agent, Pin agent) into tenants/<app>/xr-requests/.

A team's repository of prompt-only Autopilot agent definitions: the repo <name> with its scaffold (README, agents/, preflight/cases/, a checks-only cicd.yaml) and the TektonCICD child that registers it with Glidepath.

One bounded, disposable run of an Autopilot agent in its own sandboxed namespace (agent-<name>), as an agent-sandbox Sandbox with a hard deadline (shutdownTime) that needs no gateway, no Crossplane and no function to enforce. Created by Clearance through the Kubernetes API in autopilot-runs, on an autopilotReady control-plane cluster only.

Adds a deploy environment (staging, prod) on a target cluster for an onboarded app: the env's identity.yaml in that cluster's tenants repo, SecretStore requests, and a one-time values.yaml scaffold in the app's gitops repo (plus configmap/kustomization.yaml when spec.configMapGenerator is true).

The minimum AWS infrastructure a container deploys into on ECS Fargate - cluster, task definition, service, execution role and, by default, a small dedicated public network. Disposable: delete the XR to remove all of it.

The minimum AWS infrastructure a container-image Lambda function deploys into - ECR repository, execution role, the function itself seeded with a public base image, and a public Function URL. Disposable: delete the XR to remove all of it.

The minimum Azure infrastructure a container deploys into on Container Apps - a resource group, a Container Apps environment and the app with public ingress, seeded with a placeholder image. Disposable: delete the XR to remove all of it.

(attach mode) the live CreateClient/GetClient call to the Dex server's gRPC Admin API failed (server unreachable, or a real error), or the client exists on the server without a secret this XR can use. A previously observed Secret is kept as it was, never pruned.
(server mode) the Dex Deployment has at least one available replica.
(server mode) the Dex Deployment has not reported an available replica yet.
